company: Credit Default Swaps (CDS / corporate credit protection)
scoreNote: Explicit named position ('I would be long CDS'); framed as his 'pick for the best investment idea'; confirmed the trade was already in the money at time of taping.
summary: Chamath pitched buying CDS (credit default swap protection) as an asymmetric insurance trade against a corporate-debt default wave in 2025, citing tariff-driven revenue pressure on levered companies, blow-out CDS spreads, and a historical parallel to the GFC canary-in-the-coal-mine signal.
quote: I would be long CDS. So what am I buying? I am buying insurance...I'm buying protection that there is no default event in 2025...if it hits, it will be the best performing asset of 2025.

summary: Sacks argued the tariff announcement is a $750B–$1T market event (larger than the $250B Wall Street expected), creating recession risk, and warned that corporate debt covenants tied to revenue/EBITDA could trigger a wave of defaults if revenues deteriorate.
quote: The Wall Street smart money thought this was a $250 billion event. They were wrong. This is a $750 billion to trillion-dollar event...It creates the risk of a recession...there's a lot of companies that have debt covenants tied to revenue
